# Golang Learning and Best Practices

This skill helps you learn Golang by guiding you through best practices, technical explanations, and step-by-step advice. You write the code yourself, review, and iterate for deeper learning.

## When to use this skill

Use this skill when you need to:
- Learn Golang concepts (structs, interfaces, concurrency, error handling, testing, etc.)
- Get step-by-step guidance for writing Go code
- Understand technical explanations and best practices
- Troubleshoot common Go mistakes

## Learning workflow

1. Identify the Golang topic or task you want to learn
2. Request guidance for the topic (e.g., "How do I write a thread-safe struct?")
3. Review step-by-step instructions and technical explanations
4. Write the code yourself, reflect, and iterate
5. Ask for deeper dives or advanced concepts as needed

## Example prompts

- "Explain how to write a thread-safe struct using mutexes."
- "Guide me through writing a unit test for a Go function."
- "What are best practices for error handling in Go?"
- "Can you provide troubleshooting tips for common Go mistakes?"

## Best practices

- Use idiomatic Go naming and package structure
- Document exported functions and types
- Test code iteratively and refactor for clarity
- Use `go fmt` for code formatting
- Check for race conditions when using goroutines

## Recommended resources

- [Go Tour](https://tour.golang.org/)
- [Go by Example](https://gobyexample.com/)
- [Effective Go](https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html)
- [Go Official Documentation](https://golang.org/doc/)
